why_here: The evacuation package is content-addressed: tools.marshall_build.verify rejects files not in its manifest, so curated additions live beside the registry (sim/evidence/) rather than in the package's curated/ directory.
interpretation: Times are transcribed as written (local MST) and converted once to UTC. Quotes are 25 words or fewer. Locations are geocoded by this file (derived) from OSM or Census geometry named in each entry; the sources give place names, not coordinates. Web pages were read as data.

osm-overpass-2026-10-24.note: Current OSM, not a 2021 snapshot; used only to place named neighbourhoods and stores.

ignitions.time_basis: AAR: 911 dispatch at 11:05 to a line down where 'a fire had developed'; FLA: first reported at 1104. No ignition clock time is published (Investigative Summary).
ignitions.location_method: derived, approximate (+/- 400 m): east of CO 93 near the CO 93 / Eldorado Springs Dr / Marshall Rd junction, about 0.38 mi (610 m) east-north-east of the Trailhead Fire point, near homes on Marshall Drive (Investigative Summary). The street address is deliberately not geocoded.
ignitions.quote: the distance between the two ignition points was approximately 0.38 miles, or about 2,000 feet.

ignitions.time_basis: Investigative Summary: 'roughly one hour after' the Eldorado Springs Fire; taken as dispatch + 60 min.
ignitions.location_method: derived, approximate (+/- 200 m): 80 m south of the Marshall Mesa Trailhead parking polygon (OSM way/52431306)
ignitions.quote: a second fire ignited just south of the Marshall Mesa Trailhead roughly one hour after the Eldorado Springs Fire ignited.

fire.final_perimeter_note: FEDS F2391 half-day perimeter labelled 2021-12-31 00:00 local (07:00Z); later snapshots have the same area. The first snapshot (labelled 12:00 local, 19:00Z) already reaches Louisville, which burned from about 12:45 to after 14:41 local, so its label is not the time of its extent.

spread_stop.source_locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 4), The Marshall Fire Begins
spread_stop.quote: At approximately 6:30 p.m., the wind decreased to 25-30 mph and the fire behavior decreased in intensity and rate of spread.
spread_stop.note: Colorado Sun (dispatch recordings) puts the end of spread near 5 p.m.; the AAR time is used as the model horizon.

wind_evidence.quote: the result of a mountain wave that developed as very strong westerly winds raced over the Front Range Mountains and Foothills
Winds on December 30 were both incredibly strong and predominantly from west-to-east
sustained winds of 50 to 60 mph with gusts of 80 to 100 mph were felt along Highway 93 and points east to around Superior

wind_evidence.value: 115 mph near CO 93 / CO 72 around 12:00 MST
wind_evidence.source_locator: Meteorology of High Winds (12 PM surface plot)
wind_evidence.quote: A peak gust of 115 mph reported at the base of the foothills, just east of the intersection of Highway 93 and Highway 72.

wind_evidence.value: 68 mph gust at 14:00 MST near Coal Creek Golf Course

priors.wind_from_basis: westerly sector (270 +/- 30 deg), from the NWS and Investigative Summary statements above; the fit picks within it.
priors.wind_speed_basis: up to the observed sustained 22-27 m/s; in elliptical-mtt-ca the speed sets only the ellipse shape (length-to-breadth), so the fitted value is a shape parameter.
priors.head_rate_basis: FLA: about 2.7 mi (4.3 km) from origin to Sagamore in 77 min, i.e. 2.1 mph (56 m/min) observed, against 2.8 mph (75 m/min) expected from fire behavior calculations.

fire.report_lag_basis: assumption: a first report at time t means the fire arrived in [t - 10 min, t].

detections.rule: each daytime 2021-12-30 FIRMS detection is a 'fire present by the pass time' bound at the 3x3 cells around its pixel centre (375 m VIIRS / 1 km MODIS pixels).

orders.description: Town of Superior: evacuation order for all residents (town-wide).
orders.source_locator: timeline entry 12:58 p.m. (cites the sheriff's office timeline)
orders.quote: At 12:58 p.m., the Town of Superior tweeted there was an evacuation order for all residents.
orders.corroboration: AAR PDF p. 6 entry 1250: 'Decision is made to evacuate the entire town of Superior.' (decision, not the public message).
orders.zone_mapping: Zone 4 is the county's 'Southern Superior (south of Discovery)' launch area; 98% of its ACS population lies inside the 2020 Superior town boundary (50 m raster, this file's TIGERweb place). Other Superior zones (2A, 2B, 3A, 3B) already had earlier orders.

orders.description: Fire Command evacuation order for the City of Louisville (Boulder ODM post).
orders.quote: Fire Command has issued an order of evacuation for the City of Louisville. If you're in the area, please act quickly.
orders.corroboration: 9News: Louisville PD tweeted the order at 2:24 p.m.; the county Everbridge order for 'City of Louisville' (zone 8) followed at 14:51:14.
orders.zone_mapping: Zone 8 ('City of Louisville', 100% of its ACS population inside the 2020 city boundary) and the part of zone 9 inside the city. Zone 9 north of South Boulder Rd outside the city keeps only its warning: Boulder ODM at 3:30 PM listed 'areas just north of S. Boulder Rd. between Cherryvale/76th up to Arapahoe Rd' as pre-evacuation.

zone_splits.reason: Zone 9 straddles the Louisville city limit: about 55% of its ACS population is inside the city (covered by the city-wide order), the rest is unincorporated land that stayed under a pre-evacuation warning.
zone_splits.method: derived: 50 m raster of the zone polygon AND / AND NOT the 2020 Census place polygon, outlined with sim.geo.mask_contour (no smoothing).
